newsitem.title: USA: Disgraced Clinton adviser hints back in business.
newsitem.headline: Disgraced Clinton adviser hints back in business.

text.p: Dick Morris, forced to resign as an adviser to President Bill Clinton last August in a scandal involving a prostitute, hinted on Thursday that he was back in business.

Morris, who was instrumental in pushing Clinton to adopt more conservative policies, said on ABC's "Good Morning America" programme that Clinton called him just after the November election and discussed continuing their relationship.

Asked if he was still helping Clinton and working on the inaugural address, Morris said he had given his word to Clinton that he would not talk about his ties until after the president left office. Morris is promoting a book that he wrote about his role as a Clinton insider.
"Two days after the election, the president was kind enough to call me and to thank me for my work in the campaign," Morris said.
"And I said to him that if you feel like calling me for advice I would be honoured and I would be happy to help you in any way I could," Morris said.

When Clinton asked about the ground rules for Morris's help, Morris said he told the president he would not discuss the relationship until Clinton was out of office. "So, I gave him my word and I can't break it here," Morris said.
Morris was forced to leave Washington after a tabloid newspaper revealed that he spent his evenings with a prostitute who he allowed to eavesdrop on his telephone conversations with Clinton.
The affair ruined his marriage and he said that he was still trying to repair it.
